title: 4 GB device crossover: llama.cpp vs ECS on DeepSeek-V2-Lite Q4_K_M
device: RTX 3050 Laptop 4 GB, Ryzen 5 5600H, 16 GB RAM, Windows 11
measurement_notes: n=1 for each cold-start figure; warm figures have two repeats.
llama.cpp peak RSS sampled at 200 ms over the whole ollama process tree.
ECS peak RSS sampled at 200 ms over the python process tree; decode rate not captured in this run (field naming), steady value carried over from earlier measurements of the same configuration.
llama.cpp cold start = one /api/generate request including model load (wall 166.62 s).

llamacpp.backend: llama.cpp bundled in Ollama 0.24.0, num_gpu=0 (mmap, CPU experts)
llamacpp.num_gpu_8: hung on 4 GB: 3.48 GiB resident, no token for over 3 minutes

ecs.backend: DeepInfer-SM86 ECS, fused grouped MoE, expert streaming from NVMe

summary.reading: Neither dominates. llama.cpp wins steady-state throughput once the page cache is warm; ECS wins cold start and peak memory. The 8-9x throughput gap reported earlier is a warm-cache figure and does not hold at cold start (7.46 tok/s).
